### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 378c9557e725ae4644341a4c39a724b00525a387`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `owner_id (literal, 46 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 56 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 378c9557e725ae4644341a4c39a724b00525a387` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `24c3311f5604f392c966ca6dcf7fd5a80d382efa` — the merge of head `6367695ca921fee921ec01903e7db330cf19a2a0` into base `378c9557e725ae4644341a4c39a724b00525a387`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 24c3311f5604f392c966ca6dcf7fd5a80d382efa && git checkout 24c3311f5604f392c966ca6dcf7fd5a80d382efa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 378c9557e725ae4644341a4c39a724b00525a387 6367695ca921fee921ec01903e7db330cf19a2a0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 378c9557e725ae4644341a4c39a724b00525a387 && git merge --no-ff 6367695ca921fee921ec01903e7db330cf19a2a0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 378c9557e725ae4644341a4c39a724b00525a387
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 378c9557e725ae4644341a4c39a724b00525a387` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4d1H9ixhgepGZ7fawhL

**L1 verdict (L1-a): CHANGES** at head `73c5d9bc06b7a8ef93bb8d3bc7081d0f86790ed8` (announced in 7026886978). Two small fixes are needed; the rest holds.

**Gates on this head:** 55 check-runs: 45 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` both passed.

**Must-fix:**
1. **`Fixes #34689` closes the card before its Done-when is met.** The card's Done-when has two parts: the per-tool table, and "no tool's call success drops in a scenario ask round run before and after". The PR body's Acceptance notes say the ask round "is owed and is routed through the seat to the eval seat". With half of Done-when open, use `Part of #34689` (no closing verb before the number), or record the eval round before merge. `Fixes #33272` is fine: that card is fully delivered.
2. **`run_action` drops a never-do rule, so a changeset sentence is false.**
   - The old description told a client, after an elicitation decline, cancel or timeout refusal, "do not retry unless the user asks", and said `no_confirmation_service` means the user performs the action in the app.
   - The new text (`mcp-http-tools.ts` ~4759-4762) keeps only "A refusal ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED means nothing ran."; its "do not retry" is attached to `pending_confirmation` only.
   - The rule survives in the served skill, but a client that never loads the skill loses it.
   - The changeset says each description keeps "the refusal it may answer and what to do about it", which does not hold here.
   - One clause fixes it, for example "…means nothing ran; do not retry unless the user asks." Re-measure the total, since the ceiling has about 2.4 KB of headroom.

**What I checked (holds):**
- **Description strings only.** Every changed non-comment line in `mcp-http-tools.ts` is a string literal or `.describe()` text. `variables` was already in `validate_expression`'s schema on the base and was refused off `flow_condition`. #33272 adds `variables?` to the skill signature and its clause only. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold.
- **Changeset coverage.** `@objectstack/mcp` and `@object-ui/console` (public, `publishConfig.access: public`) are both in the changeset.
- **Mirror.** `objectstack-skill.test.ts` asserts `renderObjectStackSkill(o) === renderSkillMarkdown(o)` over 5 option sets. The upload-link additions are file-tool-only lines and correctly appear only in the server render.
- **Moved prose lands in the skill:**
  - `describe_object`'s field facts;
  - `query_records`' `latestPer` / `expand` / `source`;
  - `aggregate_records`' labels and currency;
  - `get_record`'s `related`;
  - `FLOW_FAILED`;
  - the approvals filter;
  - the recycle-bin restore route;
  - the new-record upload.
  None of the removed phrases is quoted anywhere else in the repo or docs.
- **The weight test is a real round-trip.** `tools-list-weight-34689.test.ts` sends `tools/list` through `MCPServerRuntime.handleHttpRequest` and asserts 17 tools and a total ≤ 38,000 bytes.
- **Edited tests are moved, not weakened.** The #32442 approvals-filter pin now asserts the same strings on the rendered skill. The #32757 read-order pin still holds on the answer.

**Notes (non-blocking):**
1. `run_action` says "never runs on this call" and "(accept runs it once)" in one sentence. The two read as a mixed signal.
2. The open-door `initialize` text (`openServerInstructions`) does not point at `/api/v1/mcp/skill`. Only `validate_expression` names "the served SKILL.md", without a URL. A one-line pointer is worth a follow-up card, since prose now lives only there.
3. The weight test's stub bridge has no `createUploadLinkForNewRecord`, so the measured total leaves out the new-record upload-link text that the runtime bridge serves. The headroom is about 2.4 KB.
4. I did not reproduce the byte figures in the body and changeset (46,827, 35,614, 17,602, 8,162). The test ceiling is what CI holds.

Next: fix 1 is a body edit. Fix 2 moves the head. I do a delta review on the new final green head.

repo:objectstack#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cxk4f4T7at3YeFruhZ

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT (delta)** at head `6367695ca921fee921ec01903e7db330cf19a2a0` (announced in 7028070988). This resolves CHANGES 7026997961.

**Delta `73c5d9bc..6367695c`:** one commit, three files, +11/-5.

**Must-fix items are resolved:**
1. **Card closing.** The body now says `Part of #34689` and keeps `Fixes #33272`. The open remainder of #34689 is recorded on the card in 7027050676: the before/after ask round, note 2 (initialize does not point at `/api/v1/mcp/skill`), and the out-of-surface weight.
2. **`run_action` keeps its never-retry rule** (`mcp-http-tools.ts` ~4759-4763). The new text reads: "A refusal ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED (declined, cancelled, timed out, or no confirmation service) means nothing ran; do not retry unless the user asks." A client that never loads the skill keeps the rule, so the changeset's "the refusal it may answer and what to do about it" holds again. The edit is a string literal only.

**Also in the delta:**
- **Note 1 is reconciled.** "Never runs on this call … (accept runs it once)" became "runs only once the person you act for approves it", which no longer contradicts itself.
- **Note 3 is fixed.** The weight test's stub bridge now has `createUploadLinkForNewRecord`, so the measured total includes the new-record upload-link text the runtime bridge serves.
- **The figures follow the re-measure.** `tools/list` goes from 47,712 to 36,226 bytes, and the owned descriptions from 18,213 to 8,500. These figures are updated in the changeset and the test doc comment.
- **The ceiling is unchanged at 38,000**, with about 1.8 KB of headroom, and the test passes in CI.

**Gates on this head:** 59 check-runs: 47 success, 12 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and all `Test Core` shards passed.

**Note (non-blocking):** the base told a client that on `no_confirmation_service` "the user performs the action in the app". The new text folds that reason into "do not retry unless the user asks", and the earlier "or else in the app" clause covers it only in part. Consider restoring it the next time this description is touched.

Not governed (no `skills/**`, `docs/adr/**` or spec), so the area lands it.
